info.title: mashctl
info.description: Speaks for the mesh, through a server: set it up, check it, make and remove endpoints.

metadata.name: x-today
metadata.value: In 0.5.5, this job was done by mashctl adopt, mashctl init and mashctl init --local. mashctl does not install or start NATS; the NATS quick-start script writes this file as its last step.

metadata.name: x-notes
metadata.value: Safe to run again with the same settings. It never replaces what a folder already holds: if the folder was set up with a different operator key, account key, server, system creds, admin creds or owner, it refuses and changes nothing, in one line of the same form naming which ('... was set up with a different owner; nothing was changed'), and the way on is a new configuration folder (--config-dir) or moving the old folder aside yourself. Someone who removes a script-made server and sets one up again meets this every time; it is a known issue for 0.5.6 with that workaround. THE SETUP FILE is YAML, and holds paths, never secrets: 'servers' (a list of addresses), 'ca' (the certificate authority's certificate, if the server uses its own), 'owner' (the first owner), 'admin_creds' (the administrator's creds file), 'system_creds' (the system account's creds file), 'operator_key' (the operator key that signs the account: its identity key when the server was set up with the nats command, or a signing key if your operator uses one), 'account_key' (the account's identity key) and, optionally, 'signing_key' (one of the account's signing seeds, a 0600 file: when set, endpoint users are signed with it, which a strict operator needs; init refuses a key that is not listed in the account JWT, is the identity key or is scoped). The operator and account keys are what cancelling a deleted endpoint's key needs. Know what this means: with a server set up by the script, mashctl's folder holds the operator's identity key, the strongest key there is, with which the operator itself can be re-issued. It is protected only as your own files are. A hosted NATS where you do not hold the operator key, such as Synadia Cloud, is not supported by mashctl in 0.5.6; mash itself works against any conforming server.

metadata.name: x-today
metadata.value: In 0.5.5, this was also reachable as deprovision, which is removed. Typing the name to confirm is what gh repo delete does.

metadata.name: x-notes
metadata.value: Order. The endpoint's key is cancelled on every server first; only when every server confirms is anything removed, so a failure there leaves the endpoint whole. If this machine holds the endpoint's creds file, it is set aside as <address>.creds.deleted, so mash no longer counts it as installed; the path is predictable and nothing prints it. Nothing else on any machine is touched. THE LATE-FAILURE LINE in 0.5.6 is not how it should read: it carries an internal word (PARTIAL), the flat name with underscores, a key id and the server's raw error. Two parts of it vary: the eight-character key id after 'user key', and the cause between 'did not complete: ' and '; run the same command again'. From 0.5.7 one line replaces it: 'error: deleted acme.demo.bob, but the removal did not finish: <cause in plain words>' with the same hint; its credentials already no longer work, and running the command again is safe.

2 messages for acme.demo.bob, 1 not delivered.

NUMBER  FROM   WHEN    TRUST     DELIVERED  KIND  SIZE
7       alice  1m ago  verified  yes        task  48 B

value.why: Administration. There are no MCP tools for mashctl.

metadata.name: x-today
metadata.value: In 0.5.5, this was mashctl inbox inspect, with --from and --to. Those are replaced by --after, the option mash inbox has.

metadata.name: x-notes
metadata.value: An administrator sees everything stored. FROM is the address a message claims, and '?' when it names no sender at all (the same '?' in the JSON); messages are delivered in order, so a delivered message never follows an undelivered one; TRUST says whether that claim was proven, in mash's own labels: verified, unknown-signer, claimed, absent, stale or forged. DELIVERED is yes or no, and means only that the endpoint took the message off the server. Whether the endpoint then showed it or refused it is decided on the endpoint's own machine and is not something mashctl can see: by default an endpoint refuses everything that is not verified, so a 'yes' beside any other trust label most likely means it was refused.
